topic: blind2 candidate capture: per-block envelope, speech/impact versus loop regeneration
asked_by: B (bab2c2e message 【三】): run --envelope and decide whether the loud tail is talking or a climbing loop
why_a_did_it_itself: B's bab2c2e script was not in this workspace; the capture B named is local, so the same measurement was run directly instead of waiting for the script

capture.rail_counts_note: B quoted 26/24 for the microphone; the 1-sample difference is the rail test (>=0x7FFFFF versus >0x7FFFFE) and does not change anything

method: blocks of 2048 frames (41.9 ms), Hann window, rfft; dominant frequency searched in 50..8000 Hz; narrowband share = energy within +-10 Hz of the dominant peak over the 50..8000 Hz energy; 300-360 Hz share also reported
reasons: the loud tail block has a dominant frequency of 166.9 Hz with a narrowband share of only 0.066, essentially the same as the -40 dBFS quiet block 2 (166.9 Hz, 0.071): broadband energy, not a line
a loop climbing at the measured resonance would concentrate its energy at about 322 Hz and the narrowband share would grow monotonically; it does not
the 300-360 Hz share in the tail block is 0.018, the LOWEST of all eight blocks
the rail contact is 25 microphone samples with a longest run of 23 frames (0.47 ms) and a peak of exactly 0.0 dBFS: a single hard transient, then it is over
residual rail contact is 8 samples, so prediction was not negative where the microphone railed: the 'model pushed the residual up' path is excluded in this event, consistent with B's reading
run_up: blocks 4-5 carry a low-frequency burst (dominant 71.5 Hz, narrowband share 0.45/0.65) 80 ms before the loud tail; that is not the loop resonance either and looks like a knock/rumble. The tail follows it by two blocks
limits: 23.8 Hz resolution per block; a loop that started inside the 41.9 ms tail block could hide
this settles 'speech/impact versus loop' for this capture only; it is not a regeneration criterion and must not be reused as one
